```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(reactable)
```

I am planning on putting in different variables that directly relate with each other into a graphic that will help people better understand their correlation. For example, the relationship between batting average and striekout numbers is one that many people do not think about, but I will explore further. My project will show the success of players based on this information, so I will eventually create a rankings system that shows this based on the statistics provided. I hope to make it interactive as well, and show the players' pictures and other interesting facts about them as well. Below is an example of a graphic I will use, and the list of players/statistics I will be basing my information and analysis on. 

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
batting <- read_csv("batting2021.csv")

p <- batting |>
  filter(PA >= 100) |> # Focus plot on regular starters (at least 100 plate appearances)
  ggplot(aes(
    x = K,
    y = BA,
    color = OPS,
    text = paste0(
      "<b>", Player, "</b> (", Team, ")<br>",
      "BA: ", BA, " | K: ", K, "<br>",
      "HR: ", HR, " | RBI: ", RBI, " | OPS: ", OPS
    )
  )) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma") +
  labs(
    title = "2021 D1 Softball: Batting Average vs. Strikeouts",
    x = "Strikeouts (K)",
    y = "Batting Average (BA)",
    color = "OPS"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r}
all_players <- batting |>
  arrange(desc(OPS)) |>
  select(Player, School = Team, BA, OBP, SLG, OPS, GP, PA, AB, R, H, HR, RBI, BB, K, SB)

reactable(
  all_players,
  searchable = TRUE,
  filterable = TRUE,
  highlight = TRUE,
  striped = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 10,
  theme = reactableTheme(
    headerStyle = list(backgroundColor = "#1f4e78", color = "#ffffff"),
    stripedColor = "#f0f7ff",
    highlightColor = "#dceeff"
  )
)
```
